config.title: Forms & Validation

intro.title: Forms & Validation
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive user registration form that collects and validates user input in real-time. You'll learn how to handle form data using React's controlled components pattern, where form inputs are managed through component state using useState. The lesson covers essential form handling concepts including capturing user input through onChange events, implementing validation logic to check for required fields and proper formatting, and displaying helpful error messages to guide users. You'll work with HTML form elements like input fields and buttons, while using React's state management and event handling to create a smooth, responsive user experience. By the end, you'll understand how to build forms that both collect user data reliably and provide immediate feedback when validation rules aren't met.
intro.usecase: Forms with validation are essential components in virtually every web application, from user registration and login screens to checkout processes in e-commerce sites like Amazon or Shopify. Social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter rely heavily on validated forms for posting content, updating profiles, and managing account settings. Enterprise applications use complex forms for data entry, employee onboarding, and customer relationship management systems. As a React developer, you'll implement form validation in scenarios ranging from simple contact forms on marketing websites to sophisticated multi-step wizards in SaaS products, ensuring data integrity and providing immediate user feedback to prevent errors before submission.

objectives: Construct controlled form components with state management for input fields
Implement form validation logic using conditional rendering and error states
Configure event handlers to capture and process user input data
Apply validation rules to restrict invalid form submissions
Bind form field values to component state using controlled inputs
Render dynamic error messages based on validation results
Integrate form submission workflows with data processing functions
Manipulate form state to reset fields after successful submission

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' at the top of the file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.analogousExample:
// Import statement for multiple exports
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported and available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' library.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react' using the correct syntax.

steps.title: Create ContactForm component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ContactForm that returns JSX.
steps.hint: Define a function called ContactForm that returns some JSX structure. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your ContactForm component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ContactForm component is defined that can return JSX elements.
successCriteria: ContactForm component is created and returns JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the ContactForm component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ContactForm component returns some JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ContactForm component needs to be defined as a function that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize form state
steps.instruction: Initialize state for form fields using useState with an object containing name, email, and message properties, each set to an empty string
steps.hint: Use useState with an object like { name: '', email: '', message: '' } to track all form field values in one state variable
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing state with an object
const [user, setUser] = useState({ firstName: '', lastName: '' });
steps.expectedOutcome: Form state is initialized with useState containing an object with name, email, and message properties set to empty strings
successCriteria: useState is called with an object containing name, email, and message properties, each initialized to an empty string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with useState, but make sure your initial state object includes all three properties: name, email, and message, each set to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState to create state for the form. Initialize it with an object containing name, email, and message properties, all set to empty strings.

steps.title: Initialize validation errors state
steps.instruction: Initialize a state variable called 'errors' using useState with an empty object as the initial value
steps.hint: Use useState and pass an empty object {} as the default value. You'll need both the errors state and setErrors function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing state with an object
const [user, setUser] = useState({});
steps.expectedOutcome: A new state variable 'errors' is created with useState, initialized to an empty object, providing both the errors state and setErrors setter function
successCriteria: The errors state is initialized using useState with an empty object as the default value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with useState, but make sure to initialize the errors state with an empty object {} as the default value.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState to create the errors state. Initialize it with an empty object {} that will hold validation error messages.

steps.title: Create input change handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and uses event.target.name and event.target.value to update the form state.
steps.hint: Use the event parameter to access both the input's name attribute and its current value, then update the corresponding field in your form state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInputChange function that can update any form field using the input's name attribute
successCriteria: Function named handleInputChange is created that accepts an event parameter and uses event.target.name and event.target.value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your function uses both event.target.name and event.target.value to handle multiple form fields.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function needs to use event.target.name to identify which field to update and event.target.value for the new value.

steps.title: Create validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateForm that takes formData as a parameter and returns an errors object with validation messages for empty name, invalid email, and short message fields.
steps.hint: Define a function that checks each form field and builds an errors object. Check if name is empty, if email contains '@', and if message has at least 10 characters.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateForm function is created that validates form data and returns an errors object.
successCriteria: The validateForm function is defined, takes formData parameter, and returns an errors object with validation logic for name, email, and message fields.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start on the validation function. Make sure it takes formData as a parameter and returns an errors object with validation checks.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function needs to be named validateForm, take formData as a parameter, and return an errors object with validation logic.

steps.title: Create form submit handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleSubmit that takes an event parameter, prevents the default form submission, and calls the validateForm function to check for validation errors.
steps.hint: Use event.preventDefault() to stop the default form submission behavior, then call your validateForm function to check the form data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSubmit function that prevents default form submission and validates the form data
successCriteria: handleSubmit function is defined with event parameter, uses preventDefault(), and calls validateForm
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your handleSubmit function prevents the default behavior and calls validateForm.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function should take an event parameter, call event.preventDefault(), and then call validateForm to check the form data.

steps.title: Create form element with onSubmit
steps.instruction: Replace the div in the return statement with a form element that has an onSubmit handler calling handleSubmit
steps.hint: Form elements use onSubmit={functionName} to handle form submissions. Remember to prevent the default form submission behavior.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a form element with an onSubmit handler that calls the handleSubmit function
successCriteria: Form element is present with onSubmit handler connected to handleSubmit function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the form element has an onSubmit handler that references the handleSubmit function.
steps.feedbackWrong: use a form element (not div) and add an onSubmit handler that calls handleSubmit.

steps.title: Add name input field
steps.instruction: Add a name input field with a label, controlled input, and error display inside the form element.
steps.hint: Create a div containing a label for 'Name:', an input with value and onChange props, and a paragraph to show validation errors for the name field.
steps.expectedOutcome: A name input field with label, controlled input bound to formData.name, onChange handler, and conditional error display will be added inside the form.
successCriteria: Name input field is added with label, input element with value and onChange props, and error display paragraph
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your name input includes a label, value and onChange props, and error display.
steps.feedbackWrong: The name input field needs a label, an input element with value and onChange props, and a way to display validation errors.

steps.title: Add email input field
steps.instruction: Add an email input field with a label, value bound to formData.email, onChange handler, and error message display below it.
steps.hint: Create a div containing a label for 'Email', an input with type='email', and a paragraph to show validation errors for the email field.
steps.expectedOutcome: An email input field with proper label, value binding, change handler, and error display is added to the form.
successCriteria: Email input field is added with label, type='email', value bound to formData.email, onChange handler, and conditional error message display.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your email input has a label, proper value binding, onChange handler, and error display.
steps.feedbackWrong: The email input field needs a label, type='email', value bound to formData.email, onChange={handleInputChange}, and conditional error message display.

steps.title: Add message textarea field
steps.instruction: Add a textarea element for the message field with a label, value bound to formData.message, onChange handler, and error display below it.
steps.hint: Create a textarea with htmlFor/id attributes matching, bind the value to formData.message, use the handleInputChange function for onChange, and show any validation error for the message field.
steps.expectedOutcome: A textarea element with proper label, value binding, onChange handler, and error display is added to the form for capturing user messages.
successCriteria: A textarea element is present with a label, value attribute bound to formData.message, onChange handler calling handleInputChange, and conditional error display for message validation errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! Make sure your textarea has a label, is bound to formData.message, uses the handleInputChange handler, and displays validation errors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The textarea field needs a label, value binding to formData.message, onChange handler, and error display. Check the structure and make sure all attributes are included.

steps.title: Add submit button
steps.instruction: Add a submit button inside the form to complete the contact form
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with type="submit" inside the form. The button text should indicate it submits the form.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a submit button in a form
<button type="submit">Send Message</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A submit button is added inside the form element
successCriteria: A button element with type='submit' is added inside the form
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has type='submit' and is placed inside the form element.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a button element with type='submit' inside the form. This button will allow users to submit the form.
